hook: Max Welling earned his PhD in 1998 at Utrecht University under Nobel laureate physicist Gerard t Hooft before moving into machine learning through postdoctoral positions at Caltech, University College London and the University of Toronto. In 2013 he and Diederik Kingma published Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes, introducing the variational autoencoder and a reparameterization trick that made it possible to train deep generative latent-variable models with backpropagation. He became a professor at the University of Amsterdam, where he directs the Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab, and in 2016 he and Thomas Kipf published Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks, extending convolutional architectures to graph-structured data. He has also held research leadership roles at Microsoft Research and Qualcomm.

quick_facts: PhD in physics from Utrecht University, supervised by Gerard t Hooft
Postdoctoral research at Caltech, University College London and the University of Toronto
Co-invented the graph convolutional network (GCN) in 2016
Professor at the University of Amsterdam, directing the Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab
Held research roles at Microsoft Research and Qualcomm

achievements.title: Variational Autoencoder (VAE)
achievements.impact: Introduced a reparameterization technique that made deep latent-variable generative models trainable with standard backpropagation, becoming a foundational architecture for generative modeling and representation learning.

achievements.title: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)
achievements.impact: Extended convolutional network principles to graph-structured data, enabling scalable semi-supervised learning on citation networks, knowledge graphs and molecular graphs.

achievements.title: Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab
achievements.impact: Built one of Europe's leading academic machine learning research groups, producing influential work in generative modeling and geometric deep learning.
